The deficit lies about 0.26 pixel from the target, away from two capable Gaia neighbors at 15.8 and 29.7 arcsec; those require about 60% and 44% intrinsic losses. next_check: Resolved eclipse photometry would strengthen host attribution.

limitations: Alternating S32/98 raw depths show that the 4.66571-day SAP search branch is half the orbital eclipse cycle. Deeper even events give the 9.33142-day same-kind period consistent with Gaia. The S98 difference image favors the target with no capable Gaia neighbor within 60 arcsec.

S93/103 raw eclipses repeat and the S13 alternative extraction recovers two. A capable G15.36 source lies only 9.65 arcsec from the target and shares the bright pixel; further capable sources lie at 20.8 and 38.2 arcsec. The target-near deficit cannot distinguish the closest host at uncalibrated pixel precision. Gaia conjunction offset is −0.685 d at the observed epoch versus a 0.335 d linear orbital timing scale; a projection near Gaia2016 gives +0.012 d with only a 0.026 d photometric period allowance, so phase agreement remains descriptive.
next_check: Resolved time-series photometry across an eclipse, plus refined Gaia-orbit comparison.

limitations: Six raw events span S10, S64 and S100, with adjacent pairs in both later sectors. limitations: Five raw events span S54 and S81, including three adjacent S81 cycles. The S81 deficit lies near the target, about 17.5 arcsec from the only flux-capable Gaia neighbor; the source is favored at TESS resolution.
